title: Treasury Quarterly Refunding Announcement (Feb 2027), 08:30 ET
source: EST: derived on the primary-anchored day-of-month rule established by the sibling treasury-refunding-2027-05-05 and independently re-derived here from api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov/services/api/fiscal_service/v1/accounting/od/auctions_query, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200) — the `announcemt_date` field on every non-reopened 3-Year, 10-Year and 30-Year issue maturing on the 15th of Feb/May/Aug/Nov since 2022-11 gives all 16 announcement dates from a primary, all three tenors agreeing on every edition. Sorted by the day-of-month on which the refunding month's first Wednesday falls: 1st-5th → the announcement IS that Wednesday, 9 of 9 with no exception; 6th → 1 of 3; 7th → 0 of 3. The first Wednesday of February 2027 is 2027-02-03, day-of-month 3, inside the 9-of-9 band. Filed estimate on two counts: Treasury publishes its refunding schedule exactly one quarter ahead and no primary names any 2027 date (home.treasury.gov's most-recent-quarterly-refunding-documents page, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 73,519 bytes, reads '(The next release is scheduled for November 4 , 2026)' and stops there), and this lane may not self-confirm a date it derived. Promotion to TSY:/confirmed is expected at the 2026-11-04 statement, 56 days out, which by this series' own convention names its successor. Proposed 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of treasury-refunding-2027-05-05; canonical file written 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research
notes: The February 2027 edition of the quarterly refunding: at 08:30 ET Treasury publishes the policy statement (the 3y/10y/30y refunding sizes and the forward guidance on future sizes), the TBAC report, and the auction/buyback schedules. Impact MEDIUM, matching both siblings — refunding announcements move the long end through SUPPLY rather than through the policy path, and no house playbook is macro-keyed. THREE THINGS THIS EDITION IS, measured (full workup: docs/research/events/treasury-refunding-2027-02-03.md). (1) It is the promotion hinge for its successor: Treasury names its own next refunding in each statement, so 2027-02-03 is where treasury-refunding-2027-05-05 stops being a derivation, and it is the scored checkpoint for FT-treasury-refunding-2027-05-05-1. (2) It sits SEVEN DAYS after the January FOMC (2027-01-26/27, federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes) — and that geometry is measured nil: on the 6 of 16 editions since 2022-11 that were clean of an FOMC collision AND fell exactly one week after a decision, TLT closed 3/6 up at +0.036% (permutation p=0.922) and SPY 3/6 at +0.011% (p=0.976). The FOMC-day effect does not bleed into the following week. (3) It COLLIDES WITH ISM SERVICES, and that is a rule rather than a coincidence: the announcement shares its session with the 10:00 ET ISM services release exactly when the refunding month's first Wednesday is the month's third business day — true 5 of 16 editions, and true for ALL FOUR 2027 editions because every 2027 refunding month starts on a weekend or a Monday. ism-services-2027-02-03 (high) is already on this calendar. The collision changes nothing measurable about price; its cost is ATTRIBUTION, which is exactly what treasury-refunding-2026-11-04's ledger caught retroactively. The naive 'February editions behave differently' read (^TNX 1/4 down 2.000%, p=0.010; IEF 3/4 up 0.529%, p=0.022) is the sibling's May artifact found a third time: 2 of those 4 February editions are FOMC decision days, leaving a clean February n of 2 and nothing below p=0.267. Estimate-labelled; nothing here licenses an entry.
